title: the Central American mythos
audit_comment: THE CENTRAL AMERICAN MYTHOS - the D&DG walk round six, print pp. 32-36: fourteen beings (Quetzalcoatl, Camaxtli, Chalchiuhtlicue, Camazotz, Huhueteotl, Huitzilopochtli, Hunapu and Xbalanque the twin heroes, Itzamna, Tezcatlipoca, Mictlantecuhtli, Tlaloc, Tlazolteotl, Xochipilli), the clerical doctrine of the elite clerics, the 20-day rituals and the compass directions, all of it on the one parallel Prime Material Plane. Zero registry defs touched; the floor holds at 995. The flagged eyeball cells: the Tlazolteotl hit points (the 2nd-print extract reads 211, the IA 1st print 217 - the Gawaine 112 precedent), the Tezcatlipoca psionic class (pinned II on the 28px two-glyph IA word against the Termux single I), and the twin heroes size (pinned 5 foot 4, the R853 foot-mark-misread decode of the printed 54 cell).

banner.title: the Central American mythos - the D&DG walk round six, print pp. 32-36: fourteen beings from Quetzalcoatl the Law Giver to Xochipilli the Lord of Flowers, the twin heroes Hunapu and Xbalanque, the elite-cleric doctrine with its compass directions, and the one parallel Prime Material Plane the whole mythos dwells on.
banner.provenance: primary ink: the extract/ddg tesseract pass (commit cd645b4, pNNN_full.txt + pNNN_tsv.tsv, print = pdf - 1, pages 033-037; the second printing); the collation voice: the archive.org 1st-print derivative (deities-demigods-1st-print, djvu.txt + djvu.xml word geometry at 600dpi). The adjudications: the Tezcatlipoca psionic class II (the 28px two-glyph IA word against the Termux single I), the Tlazolteotl hit points (the 2nd-print 211 pinned against the IA 1st-print 217 - a genuine print divergence, the Gawaine 112 precedent, flagged for the physical-copy eyeball), the size decodes (Chalchiuhtlicue 6 foot 4 and the twins 5 foot 4 - the R853 foot-mark-misread lesson, the 149px six-glyph cells; Camazotz, Huhueteotl, Huitzilopochtli, Mictlantecuhtli and Tlaloc the 15-foot cells, Xochipilli the printed 16 feet), and the Tlazolteotl charisma 24/-5 (the Termux clean read over the IA garble).

bools.name: dgfAztecMayaMoralBackground
bools.comment: the Aztec and Maya presented closely related gods with a moral background like other mythoi

bools.name: dgfInscrutableMotives
bools.comment: the beings are just as evil or good, but are not moved by anything resembling human thoughts - they act on inscrutable motives

bools.name: dgfFromTheStars
bools.comment: these beings are said to have come from the stars

bools.name: dgfParallelPrimeMaterial
bools.comment: their plane of origin: the Prime Material Plane of a parallel universe

bools.name: dgfCommuneGateParallelOnly
bools.comment: commune or gate spells of these clerics connect only with the parallel universe and the plane where their gods dwell

bools.name: dgfNoSummonWithoutCeremonies
bools.comment: others cannot summon these deities without the special ceremonies used in contacting them

bools.name: dgfNoTravelBeyondWorshipers
bools.comment: the deities cannot travel on any planes but the ones they have worshipers on

bools.name: dgfEliteClerics
bools.comment: the clerics of this mythos are the elite of the populace

bools.name: dgfAbsoluteAuthorityOverPeasants
bools.comment: even the lowest-level clerics have absolute authority over any of the peasants

bools.name: dgfHigherLevelsCommandLesser
bools.comment: any cleric of a higher level may give orders to lesser clerics of the same deity with complete freedom

bools.name: dgfSectInfighting
bools.comment: all sects must usually work together, but there is much clandestine infighting for followers among rich and poor alike

bools.name: dgfSacrificeFoodSpringFall
bools.comment: sacrifices take many forms: food in the spring and fall seasons

bools.name: dgfSacrificeHumansBattles
bools.comment: humans are sacrificed before and after battles and during the rainy winter months

bools.name: dgfForcedAttendance
bools.comment: the public is forced to attend these rituals, always held at the temple of the appropriate god

bools.name: dgfTempleStepPyramid
bools.comment: all temples are built on the step pyramid design

bools.name: dgfEntrancesFourCompassPoints
bools.comment: the temples have entrances at the bottom at the four compass points

bools.name: dgfAltarTopEast
bools.comment: the altar at the top sits east of the entrances line of the printed doctrine

bools.name: dgfPunishmentSwift
bools.comment: divine punishment of erring clerics is swift

bools.name: dgfMinorMistakesCostWealthXP
bools.comment: small mistakes (broken clerical laws, duels lost) cost some wealth and/or experience points

bools.name: dgfMajorFailuresStripAll
bools.comment: major failures (lost battles, failed quests, alignment changes) strip all possessions and levels - restart from first level

bools.name: dgfCompassDirectionChosen
bools.comment: first level clerics choose a compass direction they pray to, meditate towards, and start quests towards

bools.name: dgfEastRed
bools.comment: clerics of the east wear red clothes at all times

bools.name: dgfSouthYellow
bools.comment: clerics of the south wear yellow

bools.name: dgfWestBlack
bools.comment: clerics of the west wear black

bools.name: dgfNorthWhite
bools.comment: clerics of the north wear white

bools.name: dgfQuetzalcoatlAirGod
bools.comment: Quetzalcoatl, god of the air, the Law Giver, also known as Kukulcan or (as wind god) Ehecatl

bools.name: dgfQuetzalcoatlBewilderingForms
bools.comment: he appears in a bewildering number of forms, usually acting per his alignment but at times in chaotic or evil ways

bools.name: dgfQuetzalcoatlWorksWithWorshipers
bools.comment: he appears occasionally on our plane and works closely with his worshipers against other gods

bools.name: dgfQuetzalcoatlMonsterFormBattle
bools.comment: in battle he usually assumes a monster form and attacks with it

bools.name: dgfQuetzalcoatlQuadrupleOnLoss
bools.comment: if he suffers a great loss of hit points, he takes his beginning-of-battle form, quadruples its powers, and re-attacks

bools.name: dgfQuetzalcoatlFightsToEnd
bools.comment: he fights until his side has won or he has been personally defeated

bools.name: dgfQuetzalcoatlSameFormImmune
bools.comment: he cannot be hurt by creatures of the same form he is using - as a dragon immune to dragon types, as a magic-user immune to magical spells

bools.name: dgfQuetzalcoatlMightiestDisputed
bools.comment: he was the mightiest god of the mythos, though the claim is disputed by the followers of Tezcatlipoca, his arch-enemy

bools.name: dgfQuetzalcoatlPatronOfArts
bools.comment: he is patron of the arts and the founder of metallurgy

bools.name: dgfCamaxtliFateGod
bools.comment: Camaxtli, god of fate, human-appearing

bools.name: dgfCamaxtliSeesPastFuture
bools.comment: he is able to see the past and future of any being and put the information to use in his own way

bools.name: dgfCamaxtliNotAllowedToKill
bools.comment: he is not allowed to kill any being

bools.name: dgfCamaxtliRecreatesDamageForce
bools.comment: he looks into a being's past, finds the force that did the most physical damage, and recreates that force exactly to do the same damage again

bools.name: dgfCamaxtliCastIntoBeyond
bools.comment: the sacrifice is always cast into the beyond by the most powerful means available (a random teleport, a limited wish, or the like)

bools.name: dgfChalchiuhtlicueWaterLove
bools.comment: Chalchiuhtlicue, goddess of running water and love, the goddess of the jade petticoat

bools.name: dgfChalchiuhtlicueLifeAndChasteLove
bools.comment: she is not only a water deity: the goddess of life and chaste love

bools.name: dgfChalchiuhtlicueAidsAnyAlignment
bools.comment: those that sacrifice to her (of any alignment) can expect help if the proper forms are observed, especially for healing or love

bools.name: dgfChalchiuhtlicueTransformSavesDevout
bools.comment: the transform ability is used only to save the lives of devout worshipers

bools.name: dgfChalchiuhtlicueJadeQuality
bools.comment: the ritual sacrifice: tossing jade (the higher the quality the better the response) into a bottomless pool of water in the mountains

bools.name: dgfChalchiuhtlicueFullMoonRitual
bools.comment: the ritual is done by the light of the full moon

bools.name: dgfChalchiuhtlicueWifeOfTlaloc
bools.comment: Chalchiuhtlicue is the wife of Tlaloc

bools.name: dgfCamazotzBatGod
bools.comment: Camazotz, the bat god, appears as a huge bat

bools.name: dgfCamazotzInsectTemptation
bools.comment: he may be tempted to comply to a summons by a being that offers many insects for his followers

bools.name: dgfCamazotzInsectPlagueAppeasement
bools.comment: priests can actually appease this deity by offering him insect plagues

bools.name: dgfCamazotzParalyticSave
bools.comment: a save is necessary versus (paralytic) poison on claws and bite alike

bools.name: dgfCamazotzDarknessWeaponsPass
bools.comment: any weapons cast in the darkness at him will not touch or harm him

bools.name: dgfHuhueteotlFireGod
bools.comment: Huhueteotl, the fire god: a demon with humanoid body, reptilian facial features, flames shooting all around, hair patches where the red gem armor does not cover

bools.name: dgfHuhueteotlFrequentSacrifices
bools.comment: the god requires frequent human sacrifices

bools.name: dgfHuhueteotlPunishesWithFlames
bools.comment: he punishes erring worshipers with destructive flames whenever a whim takes him

bools.name: dgfHuhueteotlClothingGemsSacrifice
bools.comment: sacrifices are valuable articles of clothing or gems and jewels, thrown into molten areas in mountains

bools.name: dgfHuhueteotlWaningMoon
bools.comment: sacrifices are usually made in the waning of the moon

bools.name: dgfHuhueteotlStopMotion
bools.comment: during the fifty-second year the god can stop the motion of any one thing in any single day

bools.name: dgfHuhueteotlStoppedImmune
bools.comment: in the stopped state, that thing cannot be harmed by any force in the Prime Material Plane

bools.name: dgfHuitzilopochtliWarGod
bools.comment: Huitzilopochtli, god of war, depicted fully armed in blue jade armor, bright red axe, hummingbird-feather headdress

bools.name: dgfHuitzilopochtliBattlefieldAid
bools.comment: he may appear on any battlefield where his worshipers are fighting and aid them - but not so as to make sure his side wins

bools.name: dgfHuitzilopochtliNeverCommuned
bools.comment: he can rarely be called upon for any non-warlike situation and can never be communed with

bools.name: dgfHuitzilopochtliRearAttacksReturn
bools.comment: all attacks on his rear will return on the attacker and never miss

bools.name: dgfHuitzilopochtliBattleSacrifices
bools.comment: sacrifices are made to him only in battle and only by fighting clerics

bools.name: dgfHuitzilopochtliDeadWarriorBody
bools.comment: when he appears, he takes the body of a dead warrior that won great victories during that battle or in the past

bools.name: dgfHuitzilopochtliRaisedRegardless
bools.comment: no matter the outcome (win, lose, or draw) that warrior will be raised and live a long and lucky life

bools.name: dgfTwinHeroes
bools.comment: Hunapu and Xbalanque, the twin brothers, 150 hit points each

bools.name: dgfTwinRevengeThirst
bools.comment: the twins are legendary for their thirst for revenge

bools.name: dgfTwinUnderworldVictory
bools.comment: their father was killed by beings of the underworld; they went down and defeated these beings in games and battle

bools.name: dgfTwinBlowgunExperts
bools.comment: they were expert with the blow gun

bools.name: dgfTwinAvoidMelee
bools.comment: they try hard not to get close enough to be forced into hand-to-hand combat

bools.name: dgfTwinPoisonedDarts
bools.comment: their special attack: poisoned blow gun darts

bools.name: dgfItzamnaMedicineGod
bools.comment: Itzamna, god of medicine, normally appears as a toothless old man with sunken cheeks and a Roman nose, leaning on a crooked staff

bools.name: dgfItzamnaLightForms
bools.comment: he may assume the form of light in one of its myriad aspects - a blazing globe, a fading ember, a dusty moonbeam - and then may take on any size

bools.name: dgfItzamnaTravelsWorldOfMen
bools.comment: Itzamna often travels in the world of men

bools.name: dgfItzamnaSeesAllWithLight
bools.comment: he may see everything that transpires in the world if there is a light source present, much like a wizard eye spell

bools.name: dgfItzamnaFriendOfMen
bools.comment: he is the friend and benefactor of men, instructing mankind in medicine, drawing and letters

bools.name: dgfItzamnaIntercedes
bools.comment: his clerics call on him to intercede for man with the other gods in times of calamities and sicknesses

bools.name: dgfItzamnaWitsOverArms
bools.comment: in his dealings with other gods he rarely relies on the strength of his arms, using his wits to move them favorably towards man

bools.name: dgfItzamnaSonOfTezcatlipoca
bools.comment: Itzamna is the son of the sun-god Tezcatlipoca and tries to temper his father's harsh dealings with man

bools.name: dgfItzamnaCallsFather
bools.comment: if ever in a desperate situation he will call upon his father for help

bools.name: dgfItzamnaNimbusRobe
bools.comment: the nimbus also acts as a robe of scintillating colors

bools.name: dgfItzamnaDrawsSymbols
bools.comment: he is capable of drawing any one symbol per round in the air

bools.name: dgfItzamnaClericSpells

bools.name: dgfItzamnaClericGarb
bools.comment: these clerics wear few garments or just a coarse robe and carry a staff and medicine pouch

bools.name: dgfItzamnaRedHandNecklace
bools.comment: they may be identified by a necklace with a red hand ornament, and are usually excellent scribes

bools.name: dgfItzamnaBalsamSquirrels
bools.comment: ceremonies are held throughout the year, particularly at crop planting: sweet balsam is burned and squirrels are sacrificed

bools.name: dgfTezcatlipocaSunGod
bools.comment: Tezcatlipoca (the smoking mirror), god of the sun who ripens the crops but also brings drought and famine, also the god of the moon and the night

bools.name: dgfTezcatlipocaPlotsOverthrow
bools.comment: he and his followers are always plotting the overthrow of Quetzalcoatl

bools.name: dgfTezcatlipocaPatronOfTreachery

bools.name: dgfTezcatlipocaInvisibleEthereal
bools.comment: he rarely takes on physical form, preferring to remain invisible and ethereal

bools.name: dgfTezcatlipocaJaguarBear
bools.comment: when he does take form it is usually as a giant jaguar or bear

bools.name: dgfTezcatlipocaHumanMasquerade
bools.comment: he occasionally takes human form to masquerade as someone else in furtherance of one of his schemes

bools.name: dgfTezcatlipocaAnnualHeartSacrifice
bools.comment: once a year at a great religious gathering his priests sacrifice a young, perfect human male and offer the god his heart

bools.name: dgfTezcatlipocaPamperedVictim
bools.comment: the sacrifices (usually war prisoners) are pampered and feted for a full year, given almost anything - and always end up on the altar

bools.name: dgfTezcatlipocaDisorderAndWealth
bools.comment: he is a spreader of disorder and war, but also an originator of wealth

bools.name: dgfMictlantecuhtliDeathGod
bools.comment: Mictlantecuhtli, god of death, usually appears in a lich form

bools.name: dgfMictlantecuhtliCommandsUndead
bools.comment: no undead is able to resist his commands

bools.name: dgfMictlantecuhtliDarkOfMoon

bools.name: dgfMictlantecuhtliFromWorshipers
bools.comment: he requires the sacrifices from the ranks of his worshipers

bools.name: dgfMictlantecuhtliTouchDeath
bools.comment: in battle, touching his body with anything causes the toucher to make a saving throw versus death

bools.name: dgfMictlantecuhtliSpellsInBattle
bools.comment: he will usually attack with spells when personally in battle

bools.name: dgfMictlantecuhtliJadeRod

bools.name: dgfTlalocRainGod

bools.name: dgfTlalocFullMoonChild

bools.comment: once a year a great festival is held in his honor: numerous babies are bought or taken from the populace

bools.name: dgfTlazolteotlViceGoddess
bools.comment: Tlazolteotl, goddess of vice

bools.name: dgfTlazolteotlMonsterIllusion
bools.comment: under stress, rushed, or attacked she appears as an incredible monster - humanoid body, demonic fanged face, blazing eyes, talons, black warty greasy skin. This is an illusion

bools.name: dgfTlazolteotlBeautifulAtEase
bools.comment: at ease, before her worshipers, working on a victim, or among strangers, she appears as a beautiful woman inspiring desire in any male and jealous respect from any female

bools.name: dgfTlazolteotlRuinsLawfulGood
bools.comment: she tries very hard to ruin lawful good beings all over the Prime Material Plane, tempting them and destroying them when they succumb

bools.name: dgfTlazolteotlNeverFightsPhysically
bools.comment: though she may assassinate, she will never fight physically; if met with beings that cannot be hurt by spells she teleports away

bools.name: dgfTlazolteotlCharmFavorite
bools.comment: her favorite attack is charm spells of all sorts

bools.name: dgfTlazolteotlEvilCannotHarm
bools.comment: no evil being can even think of harming her, even if they are magically controlled

bools.name: dgfXochipilliGamblingGod
bools.comment: Xochipilli, god of gambling and chance, the Lord of Flowers, almost always appears as a young man

bools.name: dgfXochipilliWanderingLuck
bools.comment: he wanders among the people bestowing good and bad luck in the form of lost or granted saving throws

bools.name: dgfXochipilliPeaceful
bools.comment: he is predominantly a peaceful being that gives a great deal of happiness to his followers

bools.name: dgfXochipilliCalculatedRisk
bools.comment: the god is most pleased with beings that take a large calculated risk

bools.name: dgfXochipilliNeverMisses
bools.comment: his hand axe never misses

bools.name: dgfXochipilliWeaponsMiss
bools.comment: any weapon that has a chance of missing him will miss

tables.name: the combat grid
col_comments: The armor class cells (Xochipilli the printed -5, the best of the mythos; Huitzilopochtli and Itzamna -3)
The range ceiling cells (0 = a single printed armor class; all fourteen read single this round)
The hit point cells (400 for Quetzalcoatl and Tezcatlipoca down to 150 per twin hero)
The primary move cells (-1 = the printed Infinite move; the numeric moves: Camaxtli 15, Huhueteotl 18, the 12s)
The secondary move cells (24 the printed slash ceiling; 0 = a single printed move)
The attack count cells (0 = the printed 0, the printed Variable (Quetzalcoatl), or the printed See below)
The attack slash cells (2 = the printed 3/2; 0 = a single printed attack number)
The magic resistance cells (0 = the printed Standard of the twin heroes, the R849 standard doctrine)
The size cells in inches (180 = the printed 15 feet, 192 Xochipilli 16 feet, 76 Chalchiuhtlicue 6'4", 64 the twins 5'4"; 0 = the printed Variable)
tables.audit_comment: the combat stat blocks of the fourteen beings (print pp. 32-36) - the armor classes, hit points, moves, attacks, magic resistance and sizes

tables.name: the class grid
col_comments: The cleric level cells (0 = Nil; Quetzalcoatl the 25th level cleric)
The druid level cells (0 = Nil; the in-each 13s and 14s, the twins 10th level druids)
The fighter level floor cells (0 = the printed Nil of Tlazolteotl and the ranger-slot beings)
The fighter level ceiling cells (single printed levels read floor = ceiling)
The ranger level cells (Huitzilopochtli 20, the twins 10, Mictlantecuhtli 15 - the ranger fighter slots)
The magic-user level cells
The illusionist level cells (Tlazolteotl the 25th level illusionist over her 15th magic-user)
The thief level cells (0 = Nil; Xochipilli the 12th level thief, Quetzalcoatl the 20th)
The assassin level cells (the 15s across the evil gods; Xochipilli 0)
The monk level cells (Huhueteotl and Huitzilopochtli 10th; Xochipilli 12th)
The bard level cells (Quetzalcoatl 20th, Chalchiuhtlicue 15th; Tezcatlipoca the 6th level bard)
tables.audit_comment: the five-slot class grid of the fourteen beings (the paladin fighter slots, the ranger slots, the in-each cells)

tables.name: the ability grid
col_comments: The strength cells (the 25s of Quetzalcoatl, Huitzilopochtli and Tezcatlipoca; Tlazolteotl the printed S:10)
The parenthesized strength to-hit bonus cells (0 = no printed bracket)
The parenthesized strength damage bonus cells (the +14 brackets matching S:25)
The intelligence cells
The wisdom cells (Itzamna the 25)
The dexterity cells (Itzamna the 17, the lowest)
The constitution cells (Camazotz the 24, Tlaloc the 24)
The charisma cells (Camazotz the printed -2, Mictlantecuhtli the printed -4 - the negative printings; Tlazolteotl the 24 with the -5 alternative const)
The psionic score cells (0 = no printed numeric score this round - the psionic ability prints class letters only)
tables.audit_comment: the six ability scores with the strength brackets of the fourteen beings

tables.name: the roster grid
col_comments: The roster ordinal cells (the print order, Quetzalcoatl through Xochipilli)
The print page cells (32-36, the folio offset PRINT = PDF - 1)
The alignment cells (0 LG the twins, 1 NG Itzamna, 2 CG Chalchiuhtlicue, 3 LN Quetzalcoatl, 4 N Camaxtli/Huitzilopochtli/Xochipilli, 6 LE Mictlantecuhtli/Tlaloc, 8 CE the four - the R852 code scheme)
The rank cells (0 lesser, 1 greater, 2 hero - the twin heroes carry no rank line)
The psionic class cells (0 Nil the twins, 1 class I, 2 class II Tezcatlipoca, 6 class VI Itzamna - the R849 class table)
The plane cells (1 = the parallel Prime Material Plane; 0 = no plane line, the twin heroes)
The fixed-damage flags (1 = the printed DAMAGE/ATTACK cell is numeric damage; 0 = Nil, See below, or Variable)
The in-each flags (the printed Nth level in each cells: Quetzalcoatl, Camazotz, Huhueteotl, Huitzilopochtli, Mictlantecuhtli, Tlazolteotl, Xochipilli)
The twin-pair flags (Hunapu and Xbalanque, the identical twin stat blocks)
tables.audit_comment: the roster walk of the fourteen beings - ordinals, pages, alignments, ranks, psionic classes, the single parallel plane, the fixed-damage, in-each and twin-pair flags
